judged_text: The members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no cap (`(params[:limit] || 50).to_i`), so limit=-1 or an arbitrarily large value is passed straight to `.limit()`. A client can force a negative limit (which ActiveRecord treats as no limit) or a huge limit to dump the full member roster of any visible group in one request, defeating the pagination the change introduces; combined with the offset param this enables cheap bulk enumeration of members for all groups.

A client can force a negative limit (which ActiveRecord treats as no limit) or a huge limit to dump the full member roster of any visible group in one request, defeating the pagination the change introduces; combined with the offset param this enables cheap bulk enumeration of members for all groups.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and passes it directly to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound or validation. This allows clients to request arbitrarily large limits, and potentially negative limits (which in some DBs like PostgreSQL can behave like “no limit”), defeating the intended pagination and enabling bulk dumping/enumeration of group members. The diff also removed the prior restriction that only applied pagination params to automatic groups, expanding the impact to all groups.
